item.title: Empress Gan - Emperor Liu Bei of the Shu's Kingdom posthumous Empress who was as beautiful as a jade figurine - History of Royal Women
item.description: Empress Gan was the posthumous empress to Emperor Liu Bei of the Shu kingdom during the Three Kingdoms era. She was a commoner but was said to be very beautiful.

item.title: Empress Dowager Guo - The Empress Dowager who fought hard to keep the struggling Wei Dynasty intact - History of Royal Women
item.description: Empress Dowager Guo was the second Empress of Emperor Ming of the Wei Dynasty. Empress Dowager Guo oversaw the reigns of the last emperors of the Wei Dynasty. She was known to be a talented stateswoman who tried to keep the struggling Wei Dynasty together.

item.title: Princess Barsine - Mistress of Alexander the Great and mother of his illegitimate son - History of Royal Women
item.description: Princess Barsine was a princess of the Achaemenid Persian Empire. She was the great-granddaughter of King Artaxerxes II. Princess Barsine is most famous for being King Alexander the Great’s mistress.

item.title: The Luxembourg Grand Duchess Adelaide Tiara - History of Royal Women
item.description: Luxembourg's Grand Duchess Adelaide Tiara was created circa 1870 for Grand Duchess Adelheid-Marie, the wife of Grand Duke Adolphe.

item.title: Former Thai princess dies - History of Royal Women
item.description: Former Thai Princess Induratana has died at the age of 103.

item.title: Jawaher bint Hamad Al Thani - The Jewel of Qatar - History of Royal Women
item.description: Sheikha Jawaher bint Hamad Al Thani was born on 7 December 1984 In Doha as the daughter of former government minister Sheikh Hamad bin Suhaim Al Thani and Hessa bint Ahmad Al Thani. She is a member of the Qatari royal family by birth and marriage.

item.title: Who would be Queen of Iraq today? - History of Royal Women
item.description: The Hashemite Kingdom of Iraq existed between 1932 and 1958 and was originally founded as the Kingdom of Iraq in 1921 following the defeat of the Ottoman Empire.

item.title: Grand Princess Linchuan - The overly jealous princess who killed her husband - History of Royal Women
item.description: Grand Princess Linchuan was the daughter of Emperor Wen of the Liu-Song Dynasty. She was known to be a very jealous princess.

item.title: Women who were passed over - Japan - History of Royal Women
item.description: Japan has only known eight Empresses in their own right, but historically, the Japanese throne has always passed to descendants in the male line. Currently, Japan operates under agnatic primogeniture.
